beats.say: Five point five five minutes was once considered too long for radio.
Queen recorded Bohemian Rhapsody in August 1975 using five different studios.
Official Charts says it was released in October 1975, changing music history.
It is so iconic that it won the Best Single Award twice.
In 1976, ABBA finally knocked it off the top spot with Mamma Mia.
The song later hit Number 2 in the US after appearing in Wayne's World.
Even a version with The Muppets reached the UK charts in 2009.
Do you think five minutes is still too long for a radio hit?

meta.title: Bohemian Rhapsody: the 5.55 minute record 🎸
meta.alt_title: Why Bohemian Rhapsody was almost too long 🎤
meta.summary: Queen's Bohemian Rhapsody defied radio length standards at 5.55 minutes, winning two BRIT Awards and returning to the charts via Wayne's World and The Muppets.
meta.comment: Is 5.55 minutes too long for a song, or is it just right?
sources: Official Charts, Bohemian Rhapsody: too long for radio?
facts: The length of the song is 5.55 minutes
The song was recorded in August 1975 using five different studios
Bohemian Rhapsody was originally released in October 1975
Bohemian Rhapsody won the Best Single Award at The BRITs twice
Mamma Mia by ABBA knocked Bohemian Rhapsody off the top spot in 1976
In 1992, the song reached Number 2 in the US after appearing in the movie Wayne's World
A version recorded with The Muppets reached Number 32 in 2009
